content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents to identify all relevant project documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any documents describing humidity ageing, radiator handling, optical/transparency requirements, or simulation usage. Extract the three allowed radiator candidates, allowable thickness interpretation, and the 10-year-equivalent transparency-loss data or formulae."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard humidity constraint to the three candidates using the document data: determine the transparency loss after the 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test for each candidate, record the numeric loss values, and mark any candidate with loss >10% as ineligible before simulation-based optimization."},{"id":"s3","description":"For each humidity-eligible candidate, run simulate_separation at thicknesses 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 cm. Record every numeric pion/kaon separation result and identify which candidate/thickness points satisfy the hard 3.5 sigma requirement."},{"id":"s4","description":"Refine the scan around the best coarse-scan region for each promising eligible candidate: run simulate_separation at additional intermediate thicknesses within 1–6 cm, prioritizing values within about ±1 cm of each candidate’s best coarse thickness and including boundary checks if the best coarse point is at 1 or 6 cm. Record all numeric separation results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated eligible candidate/thickness combinations and select the one with the highest pion/kaon separation while satisfying both hard constraints: separation ≥3.5 sigma and humidity transparency loss ≤10%. If no combination satisfies the separation requirement, explicitly flag failure instead of recommending a noncompliant option."},{"id":"s6","description":"Submit the final single recommendation for radiator material and thickness, including the supporting numeric values needed by the reporting module: chosen thickness, simulated separation at 10 GeV/c, and 10-year-equivalent transparency loss."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Radiator-R3","thickness_cm":2.5,"justification":"Radiator-R3 at 2.5 cm gives the best simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c among all simulated candidate/thickness combinations: 4.784 sigma, exceeding the 3.5 sigma hard requirement and outperforming R1 and R2. The selected thickness is within the allowed 1–6 cm range. However, the humidity-ageing transparency-loss data were not found for any candidate, so the hard requirement of ≤10% transparency loss after the 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test is unverified. This is therefore the best performance recommendation from the available simulation data, but final compliance requires humidity-ageing data before construction approval.","requirements":[{"requirement":"Radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.","status":"met","evidence":"Selected Radiator-R3, one of the three allowed candidates; num_allowed_candidates = 3."},{"requirement":"Pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma.","status":"met","evidence":"Best simulated separation for Radiator-R3 at 2.5 cm is 4.784 sigma, above the 3.5 sigma threshold."},{"requirement":"Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%.","status":"unknown","evidence":"No humidity ageing data were found: humidity_ageing_data_found = 0; humidity_data_available_for_best = 0; humidity_loss_R3_percent = -1 placeholder.
